analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1030-1047), adding a description of a prompt-token cache (PromptTokenCache via LocalTokenizerBridge). The cache reuses token IDs for pieces seen before in the same prefix-cache scope, uses parallel encoding on up to four cores, and renders Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS templates through linear-time ChatTemplateLoopRewrites. It is described as equal to the unchanged applyChatTemplate path, with a load-time comparison, sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on mismatch, and a kill switch (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0). The text states reuse never crosses a cache scope. No code is supplied, so I cannot verify the implementation. Security-relevant questions for any code review pass: (1) the new cache holds prompt-derived token IDs in memory (A-001), so confirm it is keyed by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt/scope, retains no plaintext at rest, and is not persisted to disk (T-041 at-rest posture). (2) Confirm that cache hits do not create a new cross-tenant timing oracle beyond SEC-035; if scoping is by cacheSalt this stays within the same-account accepted risk. Standalone mode with no scope should be checked. (3) Confirm that the background comparison does not log prompt content. (4) Confirm that the parallel encoding workers do not spill decrypted prompts or break T-028 residual-data expectations. A docs-only diff introduces no direct regression. Existing threat IDs T-041, T-028 and A-001 may need an update if the implementation retains prompt-derived state beyond the request lifetime.
